# Snake Game for Commodore 64

Author: Stacey Vetzal (svetzal)
Date: 2025-12-08

A goofy and geeky snake game for the Commodore 64, with some interesting twists.

## Project Overview

This is a Commodore 64 assembly language program using the c2 assembler (https://github.com/Hammarberg/c2).

### File Structure
- `snakie.s` - Main assembly source code
- `snakie.cpp` - C++ wrapper generated by c2 (do not modify)
- `snakie.prg` - Compiled program (output artifact)
- `snakie.d64` - Disk image (output artifact)

### Build & Run
```bash
../c2/c2
```
This assembles the code, creates a D64 disk image, and launches VICE emulator.

---

## Snake Game Features

### Gameplay
- **Movement**: WASD keys to control snake direction
- **180-degree turn prevention**: Cannot reverse direction instantly (would cause immediate self-collision)
- **Food/Treats**: Collect hearts to grow the snake
- **Collision detection**: Game ends on wall or self-collision
- **Score**: Increments by 1 each game tick (displayed as 5-digit number at top of screen)

### Visual Elements
- **Title screen**: Shows game name, author ("COPILOT"), controls, and "PRESS SPACE TO START"
- **Walls**: Solid blocks ($a0) forming the border
- **Snake head**: Filled diamond ($57)
- **Snake body**: Filled circles ($51)
- **Snake tail**: Directional lines - horizontal ($62) or vertical ($61) based on movement
- **Food**: Heart symbol ($53)
- **Game over screen**: Shows "GAME OVER" and "PRESS SPACE" to restart

### Technical Implementation
- **Flicker-free drawing**: Only erases old tail position, not entire screen
- **Zero-page variables**: Stored at $50-$5F (safe from KERNAL corruption)
- **16-bit score**: Supports scores up to 65535
- **Food table**: 6 predefined food positions that cycle

### Memory Layout
- Zero-page ($50-$5F): Game state variables
- $0300-$037F: Snake body X coordinates (max 128 segments)
- $0380-$03FF: Snake body Y coordinates (max 128 segments)
- $60-$62: Temporary variables for score display math

## Commodore 64 Platform Reference

### MOS 6510 CPU

The C64 uses the MOS 6510 (a 6502 variant) with:
- **Accumulator (A)**: Primary 8-bit register for arithmetic/logic
- **Index registers (X, Y)**: For indexed addressing and counters
- **Stack Pointer (SP)**: Points to $0100-$01FF
- **Program Counter (PC)**: 16-bit instruction pointer
- **Status flags**: N, V, B, D, I, Z, C

### Addressing Modes
- Immediate: `LDA #$01`
- Zero-page: `LDA $10` (faster, shorter)
- Zero-page indexed: `LDA $10,X`
- Absolute: `LDA $1000`
- Absolute indexed: `LDA $1000,X` or `LDA $1000,Y`
- Indirect: `JMP ($1234)`
- Indexed indirect: `LDA ($10,X)`
- Indirect indexed: `LDA ($10),Y`

### C64 Memory Map

| Range | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| $0000-$00FF | Zero page (fast access) |
| $0100-$01FF | Stack |
| $0200-$03FF | System vectors, KERNAL workspace |
| $0400-$07E7 | Screen RAM (40×25 text) |
| $D800-$DBE7 | Color RAM |
| $D000-$DFFF | I/O (VIC-II, SID, CIA) |
| $E000-$FFFF | KERNAL ROM |

### ⚠️ Zero Page Safety Warning

**CRITICAL**: KERNAL routines (including GETIN at $FFE4) use zero page $F7-$FF as scratch space. Storing game variables there will cause corruption!

**Safe ranges**: $02-$7F (with exceptions), **$50-$5F recommended** for game state.

## c2 Assembler Reference

### Required Includes
```asm
#include "c2/c64/c64.s"      // C64 platform macros
#include "c2/mos/6502.s"      // 6502 instruction set
#include "c2/c64/kernal.s"    // Optional: KERNAL addresses
```

### Syntax (differs from traditional assemblers)
- **Comments**: `//` or `/* */` (NOT `;`)
- **ORG pointer**: `@` (NOT `*`): `@ = $0801`
- **Hex values**: `$1234` or `0x1234`
- **Binary**: `%10101010` or `0b10101010`
- **Labels**: `name:` (global), `.name:` (local to parent)

### Program Startup
```asm
basic_startup              // Sets ORG to $0801, adds SYS line
// Code execution begins immediately after
```

### Variables
```asm
var screen = $0400
var color = $d800
var data = { 1, 2, 3, 4 }  // Array
var text = "hello"          // String
```

### Data Definition
```asm
byte $01,$02,$03
byte "HELLO",0
```

### String Encoding
```asm
petscii "hello world",0    // PETSCII string
screencode "HELLO",0       // Screen codes (direct video RAM)
```

### Labels
```asm
main:                      // Global label
.loop:                     // Local to 'main'
    dex
    bpl .loop

:   lda data,x             // Anonymous label
    beq +                  // Forward reference
    sta $0400,x
    inx
    jmp -                  // Back reference
:   rts
```

### Custom Macros
```asm
macro vsync
{
.vs1:   lda $d011
        bpl .vs1
.vs2:   lda $d011
        bmi .vs2
}

macro move8 #@val, @dest   // # prefix required in call
{
    lda #val
    sta dest
}
```

### Build Commands
```bash
c2                         # Build project
c2 -r                      # Force rebuild
c2 -X                      # Build without executing
c2 -v                      # Verbose output
c2 --clean                 # Remove intermediate files
```

## Common KERNAL Routines

```asm
jsr $FFD2                  // CHROUT - Print character in A
jsr $FFE4                  // GETIN - Get key from buffer
jsr $E544                  // CLRSCN - Clear screen
```

## Code Examples

### Writing to Screen
```asm
// Screen RAM starts at $0400
// Color RAM starts at $D800
    LDX #0
loop:
    LDA message,X
    BEQ done
    STA $0400,X
    INX
    JMP loop
done:
    RTS
message:
    byte "HELLO",0
```

### BASIC Loader Stub (manual)
```asm
@ = $0801
byte $0c,$08,$0a,$00,$9e,$20   // BASIC line header + SYS token
byte $34,$30,$39,$36,$00       // "4096" + null
byte $00,$00                    // End of BASIC program

@ = $1000
start:
    // Your code here
    RTS
```

### VIC-II Quick Reference
```asm
sta $d020                  // Border color
sta $d021                  // Background color
lda $d011                  // Screen control (raster MSB, etc.)
lda $d012                  // Current raster line
```

### 16-bit Increment
```asm
inc score_lo
bne .no_carry
inc score_hi
.no_carry:
```

### Indirect Indexed Addressing (for screen rows)
```asm
// Store row address in zero-page pointer
lda row_lo,x
sta ptr_lo
lda row_hi,x
sta ptr_hi
// Access column Y in that row
ldy #10
lda #$41                   // Character 'A'
sta (ptr_lo),y
```

```
myproject/

├── myproject.cpp          // C++ wrapper (auto-generated)
└── myproject.s            // Your assembly code
```

## Tips
- Use `c2_info("debug: %d", value)` to print during assembly
- `c2_error("message")` aborts assembly with error
- C++ expressions work anywhere: `lda #(255 - offset * 2)`
- Always end programs with `RTS` to return to BASIC cleanly
- Prefill color RAM when writing to screen to avoid random colors
